entry.title: Hera 1.1.2
entry.summary: Roland Juno-60 polysynth: jpcima's Hera engine with its 56 presets. ## What's new in 1.1.2 **Louder.** Each preset now plays up to 12 dB louder, as much as it can without clipping: six-note chords at full velocity stay at or below −2 dBFS at the default VOLUME. Hera was about 12 dB quieter than other synths; typical playing goes from about −36 to −25 dBFS. Projects that use Hera play louder by the same amount, so pull its track fader down where you had boosted it. Nothing else changed: same para

entry.title: Hera 1.1.1
entry.summary: Roland Juno-60 polysynth: jpcima's Hera engine with its 56 presets. ## What's new in 1.1.1 Built on sd88me's fixed wrapper ([mpc-vst-plugins#499](https://github.com/sd88me/mpc-vst-plugins/discussions/499)): on track edit → automation, the physical Q-Links move this plugin's parameters again (before, they didn't move or snapped straight back). Controls that change others, such as a preset, still redraw the screen. Nothing else changed: same parameters, sound and screen, and saved projects open as

entry.title: Hera 1.1.0
entry.summary: Roland Juno-60 polysynth: jpcima's Hera engine with its 56 presets. ## Requirements - A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM, like the Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X and Key 61). The installer refuses anything else. Newer models are untested. - **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device. Stock MPC OS doesn't offer this; you need a modded unit. - Tested on MPC OS with a Force. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk. ## Install (scripted)
